title: introduce-cost-pathfinder-autoheuristic-prefetch-advisor
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds Cost Pathfinder advisor: a service and CLI to auto-generate conservative batching, cache and quantization presets per workload. Introduces shadow-eval mode and safety budget guards. No breaking API changes.
description:
Summary: Adds a new service called 'Cost Pathfinder' — an advisor that recommends end-to-end inference defaults (batch sizes, prefix/KV cache policies, and quantization profile hints) for a given workload and SLO/cost target. The advisor runs both as an offline analyzer (sample-based profile) and as a light-weight runtime agent (shadow-eval + telemetry) that suggests conservative presets back to Redwood Optimize. Motivation: teams today manually tune batching and quantization leading to brittle rollouts and unpredictable unit economics. Pathfinder codifies a utility-aware scoring function that balances latency SLO, per-token cost delta, and quality risk (via shadow-eval electron).

Changes included: checklist: [x] design doc (linked LIGHT-ENG-1734), [x] advisor core + scoring, [x] scheduler integration shim for runtime suggestions, [x] CLI tool `rw-pathfinder` for offline profile generation and simulated load runs, [x] E2E integration tests in perf-canary harness, [x] observability dashboards + metrics, [x] safety budget guard and automatic rollback hooks.

Commits (high level):
- 1a3b2c4: initial pathfinder core, scoring and profile schema
- 5f6d7e8: add CLI and load-sim harness, --simulate-load flag
- 9a0b1c2: runtime shim to publish suggestions to Optimize API (shadow mode only by default)
- 3d4e5f6: add unit tests and perf-canary integration tests
- 7g8h9i0: lint/test fixes, telemetry and dashboard defaults

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/advisor/pathfinder.go — core scorer + profile generator (new)
- cmd/rw-pathfinder/main.go — CLI and simulation driver (new)
- internal/optimize/shim.go — runtime suggestion shim (small integration)
- configs/pathfinder/default-profiles.yaml — curated conservative defaults (new)
- tests/perf/cases/pathfinder_integration_test.go — perf harness test (new)
- dashboard/01-pathfinder-overview.yaml — grafana panels (new)
- sdk/py/redwood/optimize_client.py — add suggestions client helper (small)
- docs/optimize/pathfinder.md — user guide and examples (new)
- Makefile / CI: add smoke job pathfinder-smoke (tweak)

Code highlights (illustrative, small snippets):
- scorer: Score = latency_slo_penalty * w1 + unit_cost_increase * w2 + quality_risk * w3
- safe fallback: if suggested_unit_cost_increase > budget_guard then mark profile as "conservative" and set prefill=on

Design notes / rationale: Pathfinder does not attempt to pick a single "optimal" config. Instead it returns a ranked set of profiles (fast, balanced, cheap) with an explicit expected token-econ delta and estimated p95 impact. The runtime shim supports a shadow-eval mode that runs quantized variants on a sample stream and records quality deltas to inform the quality_risk signal. To reduce blast radius, suggestions emitted to Redwood Optimize default to "suggestion:shadow-only" requiring an explicit operator confirmation before auto-apply.

Testing & benchmarks: Added a perf-canary workload that simulates mixed-length requests (10%, 50%, 40% token length buckets) and asserts: 1) recommended batch sizes reduce token-cost by >=9% vs baseline while keeping p95 below configured SLO+15ms, 2) shadow-eval quality delta <= 0.8% (for conservative profiles). Benchmarks run in CI are synthetic and flagged as flaky on older GPU types — we gate the stronger assertions behind `--ci` flag on the runner.

Observability: New metrics: pathfinder.recommendation.count, pathfinder.evaluate.latency_ms, pathfinder.quality.delta_pct, pathfinder.safety.rollback.count. Dashboards included in dashboard/01-pathfinder-overview.yaml and linked from Redwood Optimize navigation.

Review conversation (truncated timeline):

- Asha Patel (author): "Added perf-canary test (pathfinder_integration_test.go) to cover eviction and introduced a --max-buffer-mb flag to the CLI. Also added documentation note about memory knobs." (commit 3d4e5f6)
- Priya Rao: "Please ensure we don’t auto-apply suggestions for Dedicated customers by default. Also add a telemetry tag for tenant.plan."
- Asha: "Updated shim to mark suggestions as 'operator-confirm' for Dedicated in 9a0b1c2 and added tenant.plan tag to all emitted metrics." (commit 9a0b1c2)
- Ethan Cho: "Minor: can we tighten the unit test mocks to avoid depending on full Optimize backend?"
- Asha: "Added a lightweight local mock for optimize_client and moved heavier integration tests behind perf-canary harness."

CI history: initial CI run failed: py-sdk lint error in sdk/py/redwood/optimize_client.py (missing docstring) and one flaky perf assertion; fixes pushed in 7g8h9i0 and tests re-run. Second run: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration smoke). CI matrix included: go-1.21, py-3.11, linux-amd64, gpu-rt-stable.

Backward compatibility and safety: There are no breaking API changes. The only public API surface addition is a small helper in the Python SDK (optimize_client.suggest_profile()) marked experimental. By default, emitted suggestions are shadow-only and require explicit operator confirmation to become active. We added a safety budget guard that will refuse suggestions that exceed a tenant-specified % cost uplift without operator approval.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag `feature.pathfinder` (done); 2) deploy pathfinder in shadow mode for 2 weeks to top-tier tenants and run continuous quality checks; 3) open dashboard and ops runbook; 4) enable manual apply for select customers; 5) consider limited auto-apply with safe fallback after 8 weeks.

Follow-ups captured: ENG-1751 (expose optimizer constraints via API), ENG-1758 (auto-apply policy evaluation), ENG-1769 (improve shadow-eval sampling strategy).

Merge: squash merged to main on 2026-03-05 after approvals from Miguel and Priya and green CI.

Notes for reviewers of future changes: keep the safety budget guard front-and-center; prefer small incremental profile changes over large quant jumps; keep shadow-eval always enabled for new quant profiles.
